title: RCMP mum on in-custody death
article: RCMP are saying little about what caused the death of a Prince George man Tuesday, a day after he was wrestled down and shot with a taser by police.
North District RCMP received preliminary autopsy results on Clayton Alvin Willey, 33, Thursday, but would not release any information.
Results from other tests are pending.

In a brief press release posted on the RCMP Web site Thursday evening, police said Willey's death is not being investigated as a crime, but the North District serious crime unit must do a review whenever someone dies in custody.
A coroner's investigation and inquest are also mandatory for all in-custody deaths.

Willey was arrested after RCMP received complaints of a man acting "irrationally and aggressively" in the 1600 block of 11th Avenue Monday evening, and trying to punch a security guard from nearby Parkwood Place mall.
Willey had to be physically restrained when he struggled with police officers, RCMP said, and was later tasered after becoming aggressive during a transfer to an ambulance.
Police said they were sending him to hospital so he could be assessed for his "irrational" behavior.
Ambulance attendants had to resuscitate Willey on the way to the hospital, and he died at Prince George Regional Hospital about 16 hours later, RCMP said.

Staff Sgt. Walt Makepeace with North District RCMP wouldn't say how many times or where Willey was shot with the taser gun, which fires darts to send an electric shock through the body, causing a temporary collapse.

Willey is the second person to die after being zapped with a taser in recent months. The coroner's office is also looking into the April 18 death of a man in Burnaby, who went into cardiac arrest after he was tasered by RCMP in that community.

Willey is the third person to die in police custody in Prince George in less than two years. An inquest into the death of Darrell Paquette, 43, who died last September while being arrested at The Bay at Parkwood Place mall by an off-duty RCMP officer, is being held in September.
Last year, a jury at a coroner's inquest found Peter Benoit Prince, 64, died of natural causes after collapsing in police cells in November, 2001.
